name: exact match ignoring case, surrounding spaces, and curly apostrophe
spec_quote: Comparison ignores case, surrounding/multiple spaces and curly vs straight apostrophes (’ = '). Order: an option equal to `want`;

name: starts-with match preferred over contains
spec_quote: else the first option that starts with `want` ("Master's Degree");

name: contains whole word but skips options with the word post
spec_quote: else the first option that contains `want` as a whole word, but never an option with the word "post" in it ("Post doctorate degree" is not Doctorate).

name: only post option yields none
spec_quote: but never an option with the word "post" in it ("Post doctorate degree" is not Doctorate). None when nothing fits

name: empty want yields none
spec_quote: None when nothing fits or `want` is empty.

name: no option fits yields none
spec_quote: None when nothing fits

name: plain first host label
spec_quote: take the first host label, drop a leading "fa-", then keep what is before the next "-". Lower case. "https://egud.fa.us2.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/…" → "egud"

name: fa- prefix and next hyphen
spec_quote: "https://fa-ewgu-saasfaprod1.fa.ocs.oraclecloud.com/…" → "ewgu"

name: non-oracle host yields empty string
spec_quote: only hosts containing "oraclecloud.com" count (else "");

name: no fa- prefix but hyphen in first label
spec_quote: take the first host label, drop a leading "fa-", then keep what is before the next "-". Lower case.

name: fa- prefix with no following hyphen
spec_quote: drop a leading "fa-", then keep what is before the next "-". Lower case.

name: oracle sender own tenant case-insensitive
spec_quote: If the sender (the From header) contains "<pod>.fa.sender" (Oracle's own sender), it is OK only when <pod> equals `tenant` (case-insensitive; an empty tenant → not OK).

name: oracle sender other tenant
spec_quote: it is OK only when <pod> equals `tenant` (case-insensitive; an empty tenant → not OK).

name: oracle sender empty tenant
spec_quote: an empty tenant → not OK

name: company sender names company in sender
spec_quote: Otherwise (a company's own sender) it is OK when the first word of `company` appears (case-insensitive) in the sender or the body;

name: company sender names company in body
spec_quote: the first word of `company` appears (case-insensitive) in the sender or the body

name: company sender neither sender nor body names company
spec_quote: it is OK when the first word of `company` appears (case-insensitive) in the sender or the body; when no company is given it is OK.

name: no company given
spec_quote: when no company is given it is OK.

name: text too long
spec_quote: Else, a value longer than an integer maxlength > 0 → "too_long".

name: maxlength zero does not trigger too_long
spec_quote: a value longer than an integer maxlength > 0

name: none value always fits
spec_quote: a None value always fits (None).

name: textarea within maxlength
spec_quote: Only kinds "text" / "textarea" are judged

name: amount box not a plain amount
spec_quote: An amount box is: type "number", ... In an amount box, a value that is not a plain amount ... → "not_number".

name: amount box plain amount too long
spec_quote: In an amount box, a value that is not a plain amount ... → "not_number". Else, a value longer than an integer maxlength > 0 → "too_long".

name: work-preferences label with currency is not an amount box
spec_quote: or block "work-preferences" with a label naming salary / pay / compensation / wage / rate but not currency / frequency / period / type / unit / basis.

name: split letters match_re recognized

args.school: U NIVERSITY OF C HICAGO From 2015 to 2019

spec_quote: The card's letters may also be split by spaces ("U NIVERSITY OF C HICAGO"): a match_re found in the text with spaces removed counts.
note: Spec only states that a split-letter match_re counts; it does not define the normal-match result object's degree/graduated fields or whether 'school' is included outside the fallback.

name: fallback by degree level and end month

args.school: B.A. in Economics From No date provided to May 2026

spec_quote: the entry whose level matches the card's degree word (B.A./B.S./Bachelor → "bachelor", M.S./M.A./Master → "master", Ph.D./Doctor → "phd") AND whose `end` ("YYYY-MM") equals a month written on the card ("May 2026" → "2026-05") is used, only when exactly one entry matches; the result then also carries "school" (the entry's school).
note: Spec does not define whether the result 'degree' is the card's degree word or the entry level, nor how 'graduated' is derived from end/today.

name: two entries matching yields none

args.school: B.A. in Economics From No date provided to May 2026

spec_quote: only when exactly one entry matches; ... No match → None.

name: wrong month yields none

args.school: B.A. in Economics From No date provided to May 2026

spec_quote: AND whose `end` ("YYYY-MM") equals a month written on the card ("May 2026" → "2026-05")

name: fallback Ph.D. month conversion

args.school: Ph.D. in Physics From No date provided to December 2023

spec_quote: the entry whose level matches the card's degree word (B.A./B.S./Bachelor → "bachelor", M.S./M.A./Master → "master", Ph.D./Doctor → "phd") AND whose `end` ("YYYY-MM") equals a month written on the card ("May 2026" → "2026-05") is used, only when exactly one entry matches; the result then also carries "school" (the entry's school).
note: Spec does not define whether the result 'degree' is the card's degree word or the entry level, nor how 'graduated' is derived from end/today.
